review_items.rationale: Reviewed fixed artifact 6c55c140b1a0408fa1d92056824e1c89 (version 2), its plan, harness, claim-read-context version 1 and raw execution eae47b2a7b964503b32c9881fc487819. The increment only assigns distinct bootstrap addresses required by checkLaunchRequest; the earlier failed run remains initialization failure, not protocol evidence. Launch creates the bootstrap configurations, harvested committed configurations are applied via Peer, and only node 1 is ticked until an actual vote exchange elects it. Generated no-op replication reaches commit/applied index 4 at term 2 at every peer. State and entries are copied to TestLogDB before outgoing messages are delivered; Commit acknowledges the exported update, then NotifyRaftLastApplied reports actual simulated application of bootstrap/no-op entries. There are no application commands or crash faults; this substitution is adequate for the scoped Peer identity proposition, not durability. The read history contains one ReadIndex at each origin, forwarded by actual send, then actual leader heartbeat and follower response producers; no confirming support is synthesized. The accepted controlled schedule delays first-context heartbeat delivery while second-context traffic drains and then delivers all held first-context traffic. Peer contract does not impose a receive FIFO prerequisite; the check is at that boundary and does not demonstrate this exact ordering through the concrete transport. Each read_admitted event follows real leader pending admission, and each read_result copies an exported ReadyToRead before Commit clears it. Scenario plus origin uniquely associates each result to its single invocation, independently of SystemCtx, so the wrong context is retained rather than filtered out. High and Low are compared as a lossless decimal pair. Four comparisons were reached without parse errors: serial origin 2 returned 901:201 and serial origin 3 returned 902:302; overlap origin 2 admitted 901:201 but returned 902:302 at index/applied 4, while overlap origin 3 correctly returned 902:302. The valid witness is event 24 correlated with admission 17. Both histories emitted one result per origin and ended with leader pending count zero, after all held messages drained. The index rewrite is allowed and is not the oracle. The interface duty that SystemCtx identifies the previous ReadIndex batch grounds identity preservation, independently of successful-read timing. Source readIndex.confirm releases the prefix, and the remote branch takes m.Hint instead of s.ctx, explaining the same-history observation. No correspondence issue was found for this narrow measured proposition. Explained alternatives: Serial forwarding preserves both contexts; the failure requires overlapping queued reads and later-context confirmation in this witness. The local completion branch uses each status context; this is not a finding about all ReadIndex completions. Earlier delayed heartbeat responses were eventually delivered and did not produce another readiness record in the drained trace. This is finite observation, not proof of infinite stalling.
limitations: Observed endpoint is Peer.GetUpdate ReadyToReads, not node pendingReadIndex notification, client timeout, or ReadLocal application data.
